record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: Which fiber-wise convex domains in the cotangent bundle of the sphere arise as induced billiard domains W_T associated to convex billiard tables T in Euclidean space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth, strictly convex, bounded domain (a convex billiard table). The billiard flow on $T$ can be encoded symplectically as follows. Consider the boundary sphere $S^{n-1} = \partial B^n$ of the unit ball and its cotangent bundle $T^*S^{n-1}$ with its canonical symplectic form. To the billiard table $T$ one associates an "induced billiard domain" $W_T \subset T^*S^{n-1}$, defined so that the billiard map of $T$ corresponds to a symplectomorphism of $W_T$ (built from the Gauss/support data of $\partial T$); the resulting domain $W_T$ is fiber-wise convex, meaning that for every $q \in S^{n-1}$ the intersection $W_T \cap T_q^*S^{n-1}$ is a convex subset of the cotangent fiber.

Problem: Characterize precisely which fiber-wise convex domains $W \subset T^*S^{n-1}$ arise as induced billiard domains $W_T$ for some smooth strictly convex bounded domain $T \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. That is, give necessary and sufficient conditions on a fiber-wise convex domain $W \subset T^*S^{n-1}$ for there to exist a convex billiard table $T \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $W = W_T$.
